It supports profit/loss tracking, structural breakdown statistics, and optional multi-device sync.
IntroductionWealthTrees helps you understand your asset structure at a glance.
You can use a simple “tree” model to build your personal assets: create groups (such as cash, investments, real estate, etc.) and add asset items under each group. View the total amount, allocation ratio, and performance on one page.
Core Features:

Group + asset item management
Total assets and allocation ratio breakdown
Profit/loss tracking (amount and percentage)
Multi-currency support and exchange rates
Optional multi-device sync
Data export and sharing

The overall design focuses on being lightweight and easy to use: update anytime, see everything clearly right away.
Download WealthTrees and start your personal asset management journey!

title: Monster Chores - Chore Points and Rewards
content:
Make chores fun: chore lists + points + rewards.
Assign chores, review completion, and turn effort into points.
A clean family chore and reward tracker with optional iCloud family sync.

Brief IntroductionMonster Chores helps families turn daily chores into a simple “points + rewards” system. Parents create chores and rewards, children complete chores (optionally uploading photos), and parents review them before awarding points. It supports progress statistics and optional iCloud sync to share family data across devices.
What It Can Do (Overview)
Create chore tasks: set points and repeat frequency (once/daily/weekly).
Children mark tasks as completed, and parents review and confirm point rewards.
Track point transactions and redeem rewards in the family “store”.
View weekly activity charts and a simple leaderboard.
Support multiple children and switching between different roles/accounts.
Support JSON import/export for backup and recovery.

Core Features (Store Copy)
Parent/Child Roles: Clear assignment and completion of responsibilities.
Review System: Pending review list, view details, and approve with one tap to award points.
Points and Transaction History: Record the full history of points earned/spent/adjusted.
Reward Store: Define rewards, set point costs, and complete redemptions.
Statistics and Charts: Weekly activity, points for the current week, and recent completion records.
Family Management: Create families, invite members, and switch families.
Optional iCloud Sync: Share family data through iCloud/CloudKit (invitation link).
Data Migration Supported: JSON export/import (note: photos are not included in JSON).

Value Points
More Motivation: Points and rewards make habits easier to maintain.
More Fairness: Reviews + history keep rules consistent.
More Visibility: Children can see progress, and parents can see trends.
Optional Sync: Local use by default; enable iCloud Family Sharing only when needed.

Keywords (Metadata)chore list, chores, kids chores, allowance, family, rewards, points, habit tracking, parenting, family management

title: Pushup Log - Pushup Counting and Statistics
content:
Pushup Log is a lightweight pushup counting and logging tool—permanently 100% free (no subscriptions, no in-app purchases).
During a workout, tap anywhere to count. You can manually end the workout (or let it end automatically after a period of inactivity), and every workout will be saved. It supports reviewing history with charts, syncing across devices using iCloud (optional), and writing pushup counts to Apple Health (optional).
Highlights
Tap to count: clean interface, fast logging
Automatically save workouts + editable history
Daily/weekly/monthly/yearly statistics and charts
Local notification reminders (optional)
iCloud multi-device sync (optional)
Apple Health integration (optional; write-only)
Supports JSON data export/import

Why Choose It
No account required: no ads, no tracking, no analytics
Lightweight and unobtrusive, focused on logging
Data is stored locally by default (optional iCloud sync)
Permanently 100% free: no subscriptions, no in-app purchases

Quick Start
Open Pushup Log and tap anywhere to start counting.
Manually end the workout (or wait for it to end automatically after inactivity).
View history and charts, and set reminders if needed.
Export/import JSON anytime for backup or data migration.

Tech Stack
SwiftUI (iOS)
iCloud sync (optional)
HealthKit pushup data writing (optional; write-only)

title: 🤝 Project Cooperation Guidelines - 💡 Before Contacting Us
content:
To save time and energy for both sides, clarify your requirements as soon as possible, and provide a reasonable quote and timeline, we hope you can prepare a requirements document for the application you want to develop before contacting us.

Writing a requirements document will help you review your own project and clarify your project expectations. A clear requirements document also makes it easier for you to compare different service providers and reduces misunderstandings during communication caused by vague requirements.

If you do not know how to write a requirements document, here are some examples. They are not mandatory and are for reference only.

Project background and goals: introduce the origin of the project, the problems it needs to solve, and the overall project goals.

Functional requirements: list the functions the system needs to implement, including user interface, role permissions, processing logic, and more.

Non-functional requirements: list performance indicators, security requirements, availability, reliability, usability, and other non-functional requirements.

UI design requirements: describe the design style, layout, icons, colors, and other interface-related requirements of the system.

Test plan and acceptance criteria: define the system test plan and acceptance criteria to ensure effective testing after development is completed.

Implementation constraints and limitations: list any technical limitations, such as programming language, framework, operating system, and more.

Timeline and milestones: clarify the project schedule and milestones to ensure timely completion and expected results.



Cooperation Process
Based on your requirements document, we will further communicate to clarify the requirements and then provide a quote.
Sign the contract.
Pay the deposit.
Design / Development.
Testing and acceptance.
Pay the remaining balance.
Launch and operation.
Provide 1–6 months of free maintenance based on the project scale, excluding new requirement changes.
Long-term technical support can be provided later on an hourly basis, including requirement updates, application upgrades, and maintenance.
